newsitem.title: USA: Brothers indicted for New York mob shooting.
newsitem.headline: Brothers indicted for New York mob shooting.

text.p: Two brothers, both alleged associates of the Luchese crime family, were indicted in Brooklyn federal court on Tuesday for the attempted murder of the sister of a mob turncoat.

The target was Patricia Capozzalo, the sister of Peter "Fat Pete" Chiodo, who was a captain in the Luchese crime family when he began cooperating with federal prosecutors in 1991. Chiodo's decision to turn mob canary came the day he survived a hit attempt outside of a Staten Island garage.

At that time, Chiodo had just agreed to a plea in the so-called mob Windows case which charged four of the five New York Mafia families with rigging the bidding on window replacement jobs in city housing projects. Chiodo survived the hit and later testified against his former mob partners.

Chiodo was also expected to testify against the former Luchese boss, Vic Amuso. Before that happened, federal prosecutors say a hit squad that included brothers Michael "Baldy Mike" Spinelli of Brooklyn and Robert Spinelli, of Staten Island, and others went to Capozzalo's Bensonhurst home March 10, 1992, and tried to kill her as a way to silence her brother.

The mother of three had just dropped her kids off at the elementary school. When she returned home, she parked her car in front of her house on West 7th Avenue. Then, members of the hit squad pulled up in a black van and fired two shots, hitting her in the neck and back. At the time of the shooting she had already turned down government protection but was quickly protected by agents at the hospital. Like her brother, she survived.
